title: SLO Experimentation Lab Playbook — Q3 2026
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight playbook for running a repeatable schedule of SLO-focused experiments across SRE, Platform, Product, Observability, and Solutions Engineering. The goal is to move from ad-hoc SLO changes to an experimentation cadence that: 1) reduces error budget surprises, 2) surfaces regressions earlier, and 3) produces concrete rollout/rollback patterns that can be automated.

Scope: 
- Services: start with the inference control plane and two low-latency inference routes (text-generation-hosted, embeddings-hosted).
- Experiment types: traffic policy changes (batching/circuit-breakers), SLO target adjustments, synthetic load vs. production canaries, and mitigation automation (fallbacks to model variants).
- Cross-functional constraint: product feature owners must sign off on customer-visible SLO shifts.

Success criteria (end of Q3):
- 3 validated experiment playbooks that include measurable metrics and automated alerts.
- One runbook converted to an automated pipeline (canary + auto-fallback) in staging.
- SLO-adjustment rubric adopted by at least two service teams.

Quick notes / framing: 
- Treat experiments like mini-PRs for reliability: short, scoped, reversible.
- Prioritize tests that give actionable outputs (tuning knobs, dashboards, playbooks), not vanity metrics.
- Keep customer impact minimal: prefer staged canaries and synthetic tests before wide exposure.

Experiment backlog (prioritized):
1) Prefix cache warmup experiment (Platform + Serving-Runtime)
   - Hypothesis: proactive KV cache seeding for top-50 prefixes reduces tail latency by >=15% during peak by avoiding cold KV fetches.
   - Metrics: P95/P99 latency, cache hit ratio, token cost delta.
   - Success signal: sustained P99 improvement without increased error rate.
   - Rollout: synthetic + 1% production canary -> 5% -> 25% -> rollback if error_rate_delta > 0.5%.

2) Dynamic batching policy canary (Serving-Runtime + Observability)
   - Hypothesis: adaptive batching by request size reduces CPU/GPU token-cost by 8% while keeping median latency within 10% of baseline.
   - Metrics: tokens/sec/GPU, cost per 1k tokens, median and P95 latency.
   - Observability: add batch-size distribution chart to console dashboard.

3) Error-budget-aware routing (Smart Routing + SRE + Product)
   - Hypothesis: routing a small fraction of traffic to a lower-cost model when error budget is low extends availability without major degradation in quality.
   - Metrics: error budget burn, user-facing quality regressions (proxy: hallucination-rate on eval set), latency.

Roles & responsibilities (short list):
- Experiment Lead (owner): schedules experiments, drafts hypothesis, drives runbook (engineering owner).
- Observability Owner: ensures dashboards/extractors are in place prior to canary.
- Product/Feature Owner: approves customer-impacting SLO changes.
- SRE Incident Oncall: monitors canary windows and triggers rollback.
- Platform / Serving Runtime Eng: implements canary hooks, toggles and safety nets.
- Solutions Eng / CS: validates customer scenarios for any customer-visible test.

Minimum experiment checklist (must be completed before canary):
- [ ] Hypothesis and acceptance criteria documented (this doc).
- [ ] Dashboard panels and alerts created in console (P50/P95/P99 + error_budget_burn + relevant business metric).
- [ ] Synthetic test harness and seed dataset validated.
- [ ] Rollback plan (feature flag + immediate cutoff + traffic re-route) documented.
- [ ] Stakeholder sign-off (Product, CS).
- [ ] Oncall rotation notified with schedule and contact list.

Typical canary cadence template: 
- Day -7 to -3: unit and integration tests, dashboard prep, synthetic run.
- Day -2: dry run in staging with identical traffic patterns.
- Day 0: 0.5% production traffic for 2 hours -> evaluate signal.
- Day 1: 5% production traffic for 6 hours -> evaluate.
- Day 2: 25% production traffic for 24 hours -> evaluate.
- Day 3+: ramp to 100% if signals ok, or roll back immediately on triggers.

Evaluation signals and thresholds (example):
- Automated abort: total_error_rate_delta > 0.5% absolute OR error_budget_burn_rate increases > 2x baseline for window.
- Manual review trigger: P99 latency increase > 20% or sustained P95 increase > 30% for 30m.
- Quality guardrail (for model routing experiments): evaluation-suite qa_score drop > 3 points.

Instrumentation notes: 
- Use the per-token tracing hooks to ensure batch-boundary attribution for latency.
- Tag canary traffic with header X-RI-EXP to simplify filter queries.
- Add a synthetic probe that runs representative prompts from internal eval set every 30s during canaries.

Runbook snippets (copy/paste candidate):
- Abort: flip feature-flag OFF -> route traffic back -> call oncall -> open JIRA with template SRE-CANARY-IMPACT.
- Escalate: if error budget breached and rollback unsuccessful, engage Platform lead + Product OPO within 15 minutes.

Communication plan: 
- Pre-launch: email to reliability-all and product-all with experiment summary and schedule (1 day before).
- During canary: status updates to #reliability (Slack) every evaluation milestone (end of each canary stage).
- Post-mortem: publish 48-hour writeup to Confluence with graphs and decision rationale.

Risks & mitigations (fast list):
- User-visible regressions: mitigate with lower initial canary fraction + synthetic witness checks.
- Metric noise: use 95% CI and 15m smoothing windows for early stages.
- Missing instrumentation: stop and add collectors before proceeding.

Sprint plan (6-week cadence example):
Week 1: experiment design + dashboard skeleton + sign-offs.
Week 2: infra changes (feature-flag + tagging) + synthetic harness.
Week 3: staging runs + iterate on metrics.
Week 4: 0.5% -> 5% canaries.
Week 5: 25% canaries + decision meeting.
Week 6: roll-forward automation (if successful) + docs and playbook handoff.

Documentation handoff: 
- After a successful experiment convert the hypothesis and steps into a short Confluence playbook: goal, metrics, runbook commands, rollback criteria, JIRA links, and who to call.
- Tag the playbook with labels: "slo-lab", "experiment-validated", "auto-rollback" when applicable.

Open questions / TODOs: 
- Should we centralize a small "lab namespace" in Console for experiment dashboards? (Platform to propose)
- Who owns the canonical eval-suite for quality regressions (models team or applied-ml)?
- Can we add a synthetic canary traffic multiplier to simulate regional bursts? (SRE + Infra)

Appendix: quick templates
- Canary announcement template (Slack/email): short headline, owner, start time, canary fraction, monitoring links, rollback criteria, oncall list.
- Postmortem outline: summary, timeline, metrics, root cause, decision log, follow-ups.

Notes to self: keep experiments < 6 weeks when possible; prefer many small tests over a single large one. Iterate the success criteria as we learn.

End of playbook draft.

File history / provenance: created as a working playbook for the Q3 reliability initiative; will be merged into CONFLUENCE:RI-SLO-LAB-2026 after validation.
